step.body: Inventory your existing search data, user queries, and content structure to identify where keyword search fails and where semantic search introduces noise.
A written report detailing specific scenarios where pure keyword or pure semantic search fails, with a recommendation for hybrid architecture.
Build a hybrid search pipeline combining BM25 and vector embeddings, with fallback logic and reranking.
Test the hybrid system against edge cases – exact match, synonyms, misspellings, and ambiguous queries – using your real data.
Deploy with monitoring, A/B test against the old search, and hand over documentation for your team.

faq-item.faq-a: Keyword search fails on synonyms, context, and natural language queries. It cannot handle 'how to fix a leaky faucet' if the content uses 'tap'. Semantic search handles these but can fail on exact model numbers or rare terms.
Semantic search fails on rare acronyms, misspellings, and exact phrasing where meaning changes. For example, Apple (fruit) vs Apple (company) – keyword search can be tuned with field weighting.
Hybrid search combines BM25 and vector scores with reranking, covering the blind spots of both. It's the recommended approach for production systems, though it adds complexity and latency.

faq-item.faq-q: How do you decide the hybrid ratio?
faq-item.faq-a: The ratio of keyword to semantic weight depends on your data. We run a grid search over your test queries to find the optimal balance, typically 0.3 to 0.5 keyword weight.

faq-item.faq-q: How much does hybrid search implementation cost?
faq-item.faq-a: A consultation is free. A keyword-only optimization ranges $2,000–$5,000. Semantic search implementation $8,000–$15,000. Hybrid architecture $15,000–$30,000 depending on data volume and complexity.
